title: HBF-Sim: An Extensible HBF Simulator for Large-scale GPU Memory Systems
summary: High-bandwidth flash (HBF) is introduced to address the memory wall, which can co-package a dense NAND stack with the GPU, targeting the performance gap between near-accelerator bandwidth and flash density. HBF, however, is neither a large HBM nor a fast NVMe SSD. Its usable bandwidth depends on how GPU cache-line requests map onto NAND pages, how concurrency spreads across channel-affine die sets, and how media management interacts with the GPU memory pipeline.
